advances: Counts actual unoriented section planes of a given strict quadrilateral split. Does not rule out three different-split sections in one pencil.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The centroid is invariant under an affine equivalence of tetrahedra because the section has constant area Jacobian. Use the accepted diagonal parametrization and actual centroid formula for the given strict split, so $x,y,z,w>0$ and their sum is one. Put $K=xy-zw$ and $N=zw$. The adjacent products are $(x+z)(x+w)=x-K$ and likewise $y-K,z+K,w+K$ at the other coordinates. Thus the centroid equations become
$$
A=\frac{Kx-N}{x-K},\quad B=\frac{Ky-N}{y-K},\quad
G=\frac{Kz+N+K}{z+K},\quad D=\frac{Kw+N+K}{w+K}.
$$
All denominators are positive. The first two equations imply $K>0$ and $N>K^2$, since $B-K=(K^2-N)/(y-K)<0$. Then $A<K$, and $G,D>K$ by subtracting $K$ in the last two equations. Solving the four linear equations in the corresponding reciprocal coordinate gives
$$
x=K+\frac{N-K^2}{K-A},\quad y=K+\frac{N-K^2}{K-B},\quad
z=-K+\frac{N+K-K^2}{G-K},\quad w=-K+\frac{N+K-K^2}{D-K}.
$$
Let $M_+=(K-A)(K-B)$ and $M_-=(G-K)(D-K)$; equivalently $M_+=K^2-UK+V$ and $M_-=K^2-(1+U)K+W$ because $G+D=1+U$. With the four solved coordinates, clearing the positive denominators in $xy=N+K$ and $zw=N$ gives the residuals
$$
\begin{aligned}
E_1&=M_+(xy-N-K)=N^2-(V+K^2)N+K^2(V+U-K)-VK,\\
E_2&=M_-(zw-N)=N^2+(-W-K^2+2K)N+K^2(W-U),\\
E_1-E_2&=(\delta-2K)(N-K^2)-KQ(K).
\end{aligned}
$$
Now $Q(A)=A(A-B)>0$ and $Q'(K)>0$ for $K>A$. Hence $E_1=E_2=0$ implies $\delta-2K>0$ and $N-K^2=R$. This proves $K\in I$ and necessity of the stated formulas.

Conversely take a root $K\in I$ and set $N=K^2+R$. Then $R>0$ and each reciprocal coordinate is positive, since for example $z=[K^2+R+(1-G)K]/(G-K)$ with $0<G<1$. From the preceding residuals $E_1-E_2=0$. Moreover
$$
H=R(2K-U)/M_+ + (K+R)(1+U-2K)/M_-,
\qquad
E_2=\frac{K M_+ M_-}{\delta-2K}(H-1).
$$
The latter equality follows by multiplying through by $(\delta-2K)^2$, inserting $R=KQ/(\delta-2K)$ and the displayed $M_\pm$, and expanding. In particular $(\delta-2K)M_+M_-(H-1)$ is the exact polynomial
$
KQ(2K-U)M_-+K(\delta-2K+Q)(1+U-2K)M_+
-(\delta-2K)M_+M_- .
$
The two degree-six terms cancel, and the degree-five coefficient is $3$. Thus $E_1=E_2=0$ at a root, so the normalized coordinates have actual products $xy=N+K$ and $zw=N$. Reversing the four solved equations now yields the actual centroid by the first displayed formula. The diagonal bijection and recoverability of $K=xy-zw$ prove injectivity as well.

For convexity put $f(K)=KQ(K)$. One has $f(A)>0$, $f'(A)=A(5A-3B)>0$, and $f''(K)=18K-4U>0$ for $K>A$. Thus $R=f(K)/(\delta-2K)$ is positive, increasing, and strictly convex on $I$, by the product rule. Set $K_0=\delta/2>A$. In $R/(K-A)$ the residues with denominators $K-A$ and $\delta-2K$ are $f(A)/(\delta-2A)>0$ and $f(K_0)/(K_0-A)>0$ respectively, with affine remainder. Both reciprocal terms have positive second derivative on $I$, so $x''>0$. Exact division gives
$$
J:=\frac{f(K)}{K-B}
=3K^2+(B-2A)K+B(B-A)+\frac{B^2(B-A)}{K-B}.
$$
Here $J(A)=A^2>0$, $J'(A)=4A+AB/(A-B)>3A$, and $J''(K)=6-2B^2(A-B)/(K-B)^3>4$, using $B\le0$ and $K>A$. Therefore $y=K+J/(\delta-2K)$ is strictly convex, including $B=0$. Each of $z,w$ is a product of positive increasing convex factors, one strictly convex, minus $K$, hence is strictly convex too.

As $K\downarrow A$, the positive residue in $x$ diverges. At the other end, a pole at $\delta/2$ makes $R$ diverge, a pole at $G$ makes $z$ diverge, or a pole at $D$ makes $w$ diverge. All use the strictly positive numerators on the interval and at the finite endpoint after the corresponding pole factor is removed, so coincident poles do not cancel. The positive sum $H$ has a unique attained interior minimum, with positive second derivative there. This gives the asserted count, and analytic regularity gives exactly the claimed multiplicities. For a fixed split put the unique noncentral vertex first. Its equation $A=(Kx-N)/(x-K)>0$ forces $K>0$, which in turn makes both excluded centroid coordinates strictly below $1/3$ from the formulas for $G,D$. Thus each of the three splits is subject to the bound.

For the attaining centroid, the normalized reciprocal coordinates $(4/5,1/25,2/25,2/25)$ of raw heights $(1/10,2,-1,-1)$ give the displayed centroid and $K=16/625$. In this case $I=(1/55,37688/680625)$. Substituting these rational centroid values into the identity for $H$ and clearing denominators gives
$$
(\delta-2K)M_+M_-(H-1)
=\frac{(625K-16)(825K-266)^2(13476375K^2+5322240K-131908)}
{1910907861328125}.
$$
The quadratic is strictly increasing for $K\ge0$, equals $-30685$ at $1/55$ and $41166316/3125$ at $16/625$. Its positive root is the stated radical, and lies strictly between these two rational values. The other quadratic root is negative, and $266/825$ is above the upper endpoint of $I$. Both admitted roots give actual sections by the proved converse.
statement:
Let $(a,c,g,d)$ be an interior barycentric point of a tetrahedron, with $a>1/3$, $c\le1/3$, and $g,d<1/3$. For actual normalized-area section centroid $(a,c,g,d)$ and fixed strict split $\{1,2\}\mid\{3,4\}$, define
$$
\begin{gathered}
A=3a-1,\quad B=3c-1,\quad G=1-3g,\quad D=1-3d,\quad
U=A+B,\quad V=AB,\quad W=GD,\quad \delta=W-V,\\
I=(A,\min\{G,D,\delta/2\}),\qquad
Q(K)=3K^2-2UK+V,\qquad R(K)=KQ(K)/(\delta-2K),\\
x=K+\frac R{K-A},\quad y=K+\frac R{K-B},\quad
z=-K+\frac{K+R}{G-K},\quad w=-K+\frac{K+R}{D-K},\quad H=x+y+z+w.
\end{gathered}
$$
The planes are in bijection with the roots of $H(K)=1$ on $I$, with oriented signed vertex values $(1/x,1/y,-1/z,-1/w)$. If $I$ is empty there are no planes. Otherwise $H''>0$ on $I$ and $H\to\infty$ at both ends, so there are zero, one double, or two simple roots. In particular there are at most six strict quadrilateral section planes with any given actual area centroid having exactly one coordinate above $1/3$ and the others at most $1/3$, over all three splits. The bound of two per split is attained by $(a,c,g,d)=(56/165,47/225,559/2475,559/2475)$, for which the two parameters are $-1792/9075+266\sqrt{511}/27225$ and $16/625$.
title: An exact two-branch inverse for a tetrahedral section centroid with one noncentral coordinate
